children.translated_text: With a beautiful voice that captivates the mind,
seen by <s>Paśyantī</s> (the witnessing consciousness),
victorious is the one whose bliss is made to shine forth,
the glory of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord).
He who is abundant with the wealth of <s>Śrī</s> (splendor), compassion, knowledge,
and supreme bliss,
whose greatness is illuminated by <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge),
that invincible one is victorious.
To the one from whom <s>Bindu</s> (point) and <s>Nāda</s> (sound) flow forth,
whose nature is pure nectar,
obeisance to the one of infinite radiance,
to <s>Śaṃkara</s>, the ocean of milk.
We both hate You and praise You,
we entreat You, O Lord of <s>Ambikā</s>,
through excessive intimacy, well indeed
have You upheld everything for us.
To the one who has withdrawn the contact of union,
to the source of complete nectar,
to the one whose form is the <s>Māyā</s> (illusion) of space,
obeisance to the glorious <s>Śambhu</s>.
That which is undivided even among the divided,
and uncut even among the severed,
we bow to that universal
form which is of <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord).
From the upper half-measure of <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ),
to the infinitesimal and again to the vast,
even beyond the cosmic egg, to the one who is the quality of qualitylessness,
obeisance to <s>Sthāṇu</s> (the Immovable One).
The <s>Śakti</s> (power) that is pregnant with the cosmic egg, of the one who pervades space,
who is present everywhere,
of the supreme swan that is <s>Parameśvara</s>,
we praise Her like a female swan of that Swan.
To the one who paints the picture of the world
without material cause, upon no wall,
obeisance to that painting of the universe,
to the trident-bearer praised for His artistry.
Having properly extracted and purified
from the womb of the net of <s>Māyā</s> (illusion),
the knowledge of <s>Śiva</s>, which is self-produced milk,
give it to us, come, O Swan of <s>Hara</s>!
To the one who remains undivided even when the six means of knowledge
are employed in making distinctions,
to the one whose nature is the singular ultimate reality,
we offer tribute to You, O <s>Bhava</s>.
May we behold the deep
cave of Yours, surrounded by the supreme light,
with its darkness wiped away, beautiful,
the inner cave of <s>Bhava</s> (Existence).
Obeisance even to those who, O <s>Soma</s>,
see the Lord adorned with the crescent moon
upon His crest, the bestower of supreme bliss,
not even in a dream.
O <s>Bhagavan</s>, O <s>Bhava</s>, the desire
to contemplate devotion directed toward You,
which is capable of cutting the fear of rebirth,
to whom would that not be appealing?
O Lord of the World, let this be our task
for as long as we live:
by Your grace, the state
of having a mind single-pointedly fixed on You.
To the one whose nature is the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Āgamas</s>,
spread out in thousands of branches,
obeisance to <s>Śambhu</s>, the wish-fulfilling tree
that produces infinite fruits.
Having directed the actions of speech, mind, and body
toward You, O Lord,
becoming one with You, free from dualities,
might we ever attain that state, even once?
In the tasks of creation and dissolution of the worlds,
and in the various assignments for their welfare,
obeisance to the trident-bearer who possesses
self-sufficient power needing no other.
For <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (Śiva), who has transcended the conjunction of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities),
who is the primary object of meditation,
even His name alone is worthy of meditation; what fruit is there
from meditations that depend on other supports?
Those who have resorted to the power of the mantra
'Obeisance, obeisance to <s>Śiva</s>!'
are praiseworthy, who are prepared
to enjoy the glory of <s>Śambhu</s>.
What path is there by which You cannot be reached?
What speech is there by which You are not spoken of?
What meditation is there by which You are not meditated upon?

children.text: kiṃ vā kiṃ nāsi yat prabho
children.translated_text: What indeed is there that You are not, O Lord?
'This one is worshipped, this one is meditated upon,
this one is pleased' — may this
<s>rasa</s> (sentiment) toward You, O <s>Bhava</s>,
grow in me through a thousand streams.
Obeisance to the one whose nature is the abode
of garlands of all the wings of intellect,
to the Lord, to <s>Sthāṇu</s>, to You
who wears a serpent as the sacred thread.
The sole remedy for the darkness of ignorance
is the remembrance of You;
O <s>Bhava</s>, through the gift of that very thing,
let Your grace be bestowed upon me.
Obeisance to the Lord; the one who accomplishes
all the aims of human life completely,
even the act of bowing to whom
is worthy of being bowed to by the wise.
For those drowning in the terrible ocean of worldly existence,
the abode of the sea-creatures of suffering,
having then obtained the wish-fulfilling gem of devotion to <s>Śarva</s> (Śiva),
what has not been conquered?
You are to be known by those who possess the wealth of knowledge
that is unveiled, free from dualities, and unwavering;
who indeed are those rare ones
who know You, O <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>?
Though without qualities, He alone is to be known by the knowers of qualities,
victorious is the unborn one;
though by nature desireless,
He is the supreme fruit for those who desire.
That for which the gods toiled
to obtain the splendid jewel of nectar,
that sovereignty of the milk-ocean
is innately Yours alone, O all-pervading Lord.
Obeisance through devotion; for the liberation of people,
to <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva), who protects,
who gives through remembrance and praise,
to <s>Śambhu</s>, who creates welfare, who is beyond becoming.
You are omniscient, the maker of all, You are everything —
thus for those endowed with knowledge,
what is there to be known, or what action, O Lord,
is not offered to You for the sake of infinity?
He whose mere will
has as its fruit the three worlds,
of You, O Lord, who knows
how vast is the reach of Your purposes?
Even <s>Brahmā</s> and others rush
upward and upward on the stairway of actions
to attain that abode of His;
I bow to Him.
'This is <s>Brahmā</s>, this is great <s>Indra</s>,
these are <s>Sūrya</s> and <s>Candra</s>' —
thus has the creeper of His <s>Śakti</s> (power)
blossomed; may that <s>Bhava</s> protect us.
He whose measure cannot be found
even by the wandering inner faculties,
whose end is unreachable even by those who travel far,
hard to reach — we praise <s>Mṛḍa</s> (the Gracious One).
Obeisance in praise, in remembrance, in meditation,
in seeing, in touching,
and in attainment — to the mass of bliss,
to the beloved <s>Kapardin</s> (the Matted-Haired One).
'What use is pride?' — even thinking thus,
O <s>Parameśvara</s>, in my mind,
through the pride that 'I am one with You,'
do I not delight within myself with joy?
Even after contemplating millions of tasks
due to the fickleness of the mind,
resting, O <s>Bhava</s>, in the bliss of the mind
directed toward You, I delight greatly.
If You are subtle, how can these three worlds
be merely a fraction of You?
If then You are gross, why are You not easily seen
even by <s>Brahmā</s> and others, O Lord?
If it were not the case that You are the one
to be expressed by all these words,
what wise person, O God, would have undertaken
the trouble of weaving nets of words?
By what gradual process, by what action,
or by what wisdom, O Lord,
are You to be seen? — through such instruction,
let grace be bestowed upon me.
Obeisance to the one who has nothing to accomplish for Himself,
yet is the sole benefactor of the three worlds,
who is desirable to all,
yet Himself free from desire — to <s>Kapardin</s>.
Ah, this quality of being a knower of the field
serves a great purpose for the righteous,
by which they sow the seeds of devotion bearing infinite fruit
in You, O Lord.
Ah, how great is this <s>Māyā</s> (illusion) of Yours,
O wielder of <s>Māyā</s>, by which, though enveloped,
even when the treasure of meditation on You is available,
the deluded world grows slack.
Whether it be action or instrument or anything else,
in every beginning, O <s>Bhava</s>,
let the universe exist; but the independent
agent therein is You alone.
The three worlds, caught in the dualities
of the three <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and their triple vibrations,
who other than You has the power
or the compassion to uplift them?
Even a fault, O God, what fault is it
if it is employed in attaining You?
And even a virtue, what virtue is it indeed
if it is not employed in attaining You?
Let there even be attachment, O Lord of the World,
if mine is fixed in You alone;
obeisance even to that greed of mine
which has as its object the attainment of You.
Ah, how great is this action
consisting of meditation on You, O God,
in which, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a worm,
who would not be eligible for liberation?
The beginning of all undertakings,
the culmination of all actions,
and the wondrous mental states in between —
all are on the path of Your intellect alone, O Lord.
An ever-increasing relish
expanding a thousandfold in its savor,
the nectar of the <s>rasa</s> (essence) of devotion to You,
O Lord, is not found elsewhere.
To the one who has withdrawn desires yet extends the reach of desires,
to the one who expands the dominion of <s>Kāma</s> (desire),
to the one adorned with the crescent moon,
obeisance to <s>Soma</s>, the sovereign Lord.
'What can I do, being powerless?' —
for one who lacks resolve everywhere,
the all-gracious power of <s>Śaṃkara</s>
is my refuge.
Of You who have transcended the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), whose nature
is proclaimed as surpassing all in every respect,
O <s>Bhava</s>, where in any part
can a supreme substitute for You be found?
Though You are without dualities and without limiting conditions,
and are the Self itself, O Lord,
we are still being deceived even now
by Your immeasurable <s>Māyā</s> (illusion).
The attainment of <s>aṇimā</s> (power of becoming minute) and other qualities,
eternal sovereignty, the destruction of worldly existence —
these, O <s>Bhava</s>, are the tender shoots
of the wish-fulfilling tree of devotion to You.

children.text: yā yā dik tatra na kvāsi
children.translated_text: In whatever direction — there is nowhere You are not;
every moment is filled with You;
thus, though already obtained, when
shall You be attained? Tell us, O Lord.
Obeisance to the one who dwells solely in the minds
of the serene and virtuous,
whose body is whitened with abundant sacred ash,
to the great Swan, to <s>Śambhu</s>.
May the lamp of knowledge of You, having removed the darkness of pride
and burned all the fuel of worldly existence,
be mine, O Lord —
that lamp which is devotion to You.
Having released the drama of the three worlds,
pregnant with many excellent seeds,
to set it on stage and then to dissolve it, O <s>Hara</s>,
what other poet besides You is capable?
Obeisance to the one who is independent yet not independent,
capable of rendering the existent non-existent
or the non-existent into existence,
who alone possesses the sovereignty of expenditure.
Whatever bliss of any kind
is seen in all the three worlds,
that is but a drop of His; I worship
that God, the ocean of bliss.
Ah, blessed are <s>Brahmā</s> and others
who, freed from all other doubts,
chant 'Obeisance, obeisance to <s>Śiva</s>!'
overwhelmed with delight.
Though desireless, to the bestower
of infinite desires,
though beginningless, to the enjoyer
of the universe — O <s>Bhava</s>, obeisance to You.
We praise the Lord who is the primal <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature),
the root of the creation of the three worlds;
who would not seek a favor
from one whose dharma is complete?
Even in great calamities of purpose,
when minds are muddied by the flood of delusion,
when He is remembered, they become clear —
we praise that <s>Śiva</s>.
O Lord, Yours alone here
is the unbreakable power of lordship,
by whose will
the dissolution and creation of the three worlds are extended.
Even a wicked deed, when dedicated to the God,
becomes the highest merit;
and the merit of merit itself
comes from no other — You are that, O Lord.
'Here, You are seized with my fist!
Here, You are seen! Where will You go from us?'
Thus, inflated with the <s>rasa</s> (essence) of devotion,
the blessed ones run toward <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>.
We praise You, the supreme beyond the essence
of the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> Vedas,
whose Veda-natured consort, unfathomable,
is, ah, profoundly beautiful.
You are the ordinance, the beginning, and likewise the end
of the universe, O <s>Parameśvara</s>;
the totality of <s>dharma</s> that has arisen
from You — from where else could it come?
Obeisance to You who, bringing to light the confusion
of those bewildered by worldly existence, shatter it,
and then bestow the knowledge-bliss
that is free from dualities, O God.
By what desires could the ultimate limit
of that <s>Māyā</s> (illusion) be reached?
May <s>Śiva</s>, who steals it away
in a single moment, protect us.
The profound course of <s>Vairāgya</s> (dispassion),
the supreme glory of <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge),
the ultimate pinnacle of desirelessness —
of those who bear these, You, O Lord, are the Lord.
You are the <s>Brahman</s> (Absolute) even of <s>Brahmā</s>;
of what ruler are You not the Lord?
The auspiciousness of the world's auspiciousness —
who knows how vast You are?
What need of other relatives, or
of friends and masters?
In every situation, O Lord, You are mine,
You who deliver from the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence).
Victorious are the divine drops of nectar,
capable of washing away the stains of delusion, <s>Māyā</s>, and the rest,
drawn forth by the power of <s>Śaiva</s> <s>Yoga</s>,
those celestial sprinklings of ambrosia.
He whose light that inspires thoughts
is sung by the <s>Gāyatrī</s>,
may that Lord also guide
our minds on the righteous path.
O <s>Aṣṭamūrti</s> (eight-formed one), will You not grant us
eternal abiding even in one of Your forms?
Or rather, if pleased,
You will grant everything.
The essential truth of objects
generally produces practical results;
but Your very name, O Lord,
grants accomplishment up to <s>Mokṣa</s> (liberation).
That power of Yours by which, again and again,
You devise ever-new states for the wondrous painting of the world,
O Lord, by that power
what wise person is not astonished?
To make the difficult easy,
and to turn suffering into happiness,
the sole heroic force is the remembrance of Him —
we remember that enemy of <s>Smara</s> (Kāma, the god of love).
Victorious are those songs
whose subject of singing is <s>Parameśvara</s>,
by whose mere name the great souls
are covered with horripilation.
If there were one like You,
or rather, only You Yourself could be, O <s>Bhava</s>,
the one who, arrayed with the host of His own powers,
effects the creation and dissolution of the three worlds.
You are the <s>Mantra</s> (sacred formula), You are to be consulted,
what counselor is there other than You?
Give me that <s>Mantra</s>,
so that I may become Your <s>Mantra</s>, O Lord.
You are of the form of light, of true resolve;
I too am one whose Self is You;
that I am a <s>saṃsārin</s> (worldly being), O Lord, is this
a dream? And whence could even that dream arise in You?
That is unbreakable, that is not vulgar,
that is singular and well-established —
the sovereignty, O Lord, that comes from
the offering of the fruits of action to You.
What misfortune is He not capable of destroying?
What prosperity is He not able to bestow?
He who is such is our beloved,
the God of gods, <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s> (the Bull-bannered One).
For the one blinded by the impurity of the stain of <s>Māyā</s> (illusion),
for purifying the divine eye of knowledge,
O Lord,
devotion to You is the supreme collyrium.
That which is fearless, that which is full
of bliss, that which is one and imperishable —
grant me that state, come, O God,
quickly! Why do You delay?
Ah, the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) is naturally deep
and terrible;
ah, the supreme means for crossing it
is none other than <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord).
Obeisance to You who have put an end to the Ender (Death),
O crusher of <s>Madana</s> (the god of love),
who bears the <s>Gaṅgā</s> upon His head,
who acts in accordance with what is fitting.
For those who aspire to a state
even beyond sovereignty, knowledge, dispassion, and <s>dharma</s>,
O Lord, for those who pray thus,
what higher refuge is there besides You?
O <s>Śambhu</s>, when You do not will it, who has the power
to bend even a blade of grass?
But favored by Your will,
who could not bear the yoke of <s>Brahmā</s> (cosmic creation)?
Those whose distinguished heads, with jeweled crowns,
are bowed in prostration to <s>Hara</s>,
to what higher being would they bow,
or whom would they not cause to bow — those rich in wisdom?
The shedding of all delusion,
the unshakable pool of nectar,
the center of the ocean of knowledge that is You —
may I dwell therein, O <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s>.
Wondrous it is that even when seen in a painting
or merely imagined in a wish,
O Lord, You bestow
the full fruit of the ultimate reality.
Who surpasses You in qualities?
Who surpasses You in being without qualities?
Thus, O Lord, shall we praise You
or shall we blame You? We cannot decide.
Even in the mere chanting, the fruit
of Your gracious satisfaction is a flood of nectar;
who else is capable of even drinking that,
let alone bestowing it, O Lord of the World?
From being the treasury that accomplishes
the meaningful fulfillment of all that is to be sought,
From you, your devotion alone
I pray for in every way, O Lord!
Homage to you, the Lord of the three worlds,
O <s>Bhava</s>, for those devoted to you —
to you whose power removes obstacles
in granting lordship over the three worlds.
When there is doubt: 'What is the cause
of the complete destruction of afflictions?' —
having ascertained 'O Lord, you are that [cause]!' —
who would not take refuge in you?
Having enjoyed pleasures and abandoned the delusion of existence,
I shall attain the supreme state —
thus to aspire would be surpassed
only by devotion to <s>Śambhu</s>.
O Lord, whatever I may do
or say, even in a dream, whether good or bad,
by the pride of being under your authority,
I am at peace in all things, free from fear.
That light which is the light even of [all] lights —
when the mind rushes toward your abode,
I think its touch of darkness, O Lord,
is [as impossible as] the younger brother of a barren woman's son.
I consider that even the wish
'I shall serve <s>Śiva</s>' —
one who holds this aspiration has his foot placed
upon the safe path of liberation.
In the maintenance, creation, and dissolution
of the three worlds, in these benefactions —
your power alone, O Lord, operates —
you who behold an independent system.
In the three worlds, who here is protected,
not afflicted by the three sufferings?
Homage to you for that — you who are
the lake of the nectar of that cessation (<s>nirvāṇa</s>)!
Even artificial devotion to you
yields genuine fruits;
if it were without pretense,
what its fruit would be — let that be declared by you!
That eye by which you are seen,
that path by which you are reached —
that fruit, O Unborn One, has arisen
from the wish-fulfilling tree of stories about you.
This itself is the good of all goods:
that abiding in you above [all else];
for the removal of obstacles to that,
you, O Lord, are my refuge.
Oh, how supremely sweet, O <s>Śarva</s>,
is the nectar-stream of aspiring to your service!
At what point in even the minutest fraction of time
does it not become ever new?
Again and again, tirelessly,
creating the three worlds with hundreds of creations —
some One, though creating,
remains free from modification — the Unborn One triumphs!
With the lamp of knowledge that burns away
the tendencies — the rotating wick of <s>saṃsāra</s>
soaked in the oil of impurity —
O God, when shall I be established before you?
If for even a single moment
you place your foot
in the mind whose faults are destroyed — then, O <s>Śambhu</s>,
what will you not accomplish?
'I am blessed! I have achieved my purpose!
I am great!' — such a contemplation
would have its support
for one whose support is you, O Lord.
Of all that is auspicious and inauspicious,
you yourself are the maker, O <s>Bhava</s>;
but devotion to you, O Lord, is the mother
of the auspicious alone.
O Master, do you enter a serene mind,
or does the mind become serene
from your entering it? —
thus people oscillate [in doubt].
But the conclusion here is this:
it is indeed your presence [that causes it];
the serenity of the mind, O Master,
is that perfection, that supreme state.
My speech, my mind, my actions,
and my body, O Lord —
by your grace, may they become
adorned solely by devotion to you.
This <s>Stavacintāmaṇi</s> (Wish-fulfilling Gem of Praise),
which abundantly grants the fruits of all desires,
the abode of the splendor of devotion — O <s>Śambhu</s>,
<s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s> has composed [it].
He triumphs, the Supreme Lord, whose glory of manifested bliss is [revealed] by the beautiful, mind-captivating, seeing and visible <s>parā vāk</s> (supreme speech). ||
He triumphs, the Unconquered One, who is rich with the wealth of prosperity, compassion, knowledge, and supreme bliss, whose greatness is illuminated by <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge). ||
Homage to <s>Śaṃkara</s>, the ocean of milk, of spreading <s>bindu</s> and <s>nāda</s>, whose nature is pure nectar, of infinite radiance. ||
We hate you, we praise you, we invoke you, O Husband of <s>Ambikā</s>! Through exceeding accessibility, you have well held us in all directions. ||
Homage to <s>Śambhu</s>, the glorious one, whose contact with [material] touch has been withdrawn, who is the source of complete nectar, whose nature is the <s>māyā</s> of space. ||
We bow to that universal form of the Supreme Lord — that which is undivided even in what is divided, uncut even in what is cut. ||
Smaller even than the upper <s>mātrā</s> (measure) of <s>praṇava</s> (Oṃ), yet greater than the cosmic egg — homage to <s>Sthāṇu</s>, whose qualities are [those of] attributelessness! ||
We praise the <s>Śakti</s> (power) of the Supreme Lord, the Swan that pervades space and is present everywhere — [his Śakti] who is like the female swan [to him], pregnant with the cosmic egg. ||
Homage to the Trident-bearer, praiseworthy in [his] art, who paints the picture of the world upon no [material] wall, without material cause! ||
O <s>Hara</s>-Swan! Having properly extracted and purified from the belly of the net of <s>māyā</s>, give us the <s>Śiva</s>-knowledge, the milk [that flows] naturally — come! ||
To you, <s>Bhava</s>, whose nature is the one reality though [analyzed by] the six means of knowledge with their divisions and distinctions — we offer tribute. ||
May we see that deep, beautiful cave of yours within, O <s>Bhava</s>, illuminated all around by the supreme light, its darkness wiped away! ||
Homage even to those who behold, even in a dream, the Lord whose crest is adorned with the digits of the moon, the bestower of supreme bliss. ||
O <s>Bhagavān</s>, O <s>Bhava</s>! There is a desire to contemplate devotion directed toward you; who would not delight in that which is capable of destroying the fear of rebirth? ||
O Lord of the World, may this be our lifelong duty: that state — by your grace — of having the mind single-pointedly [fixed] on you alone. ||
Homage to <s>Śambhu</s>, whose nature is the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Āgamas</s> spreading in thousands of branches, the wish-fulfilling tree producing endless fruits. ||
You alone, O <s>Hara</s>, the greatest, are the proper receptacle in the universe for the offering of our devotion — for others are not free from desire [for its fruits]. ||

We worship the primal Lord who, though free from desire, creates all that is desirable — the source of the cosmic <s>icchā</s> (will), <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), and <s>kriyā</s> (action) <s>śaktis</s>. ||
We worship the Lord who, though motionless, is present everywhere like space; who though formless, delights [all beings] with [his] form. ||
Even the enemies of <s>Hara</s>, at the time of the great dissolution, praise [him]; what wonder that those devoted to him praise [him] always? ||

children.text: kas+panthās+yena na prāpyas+kā ca vāk+na+ucyase yayā |
children.translated_text: May that supreme light of the eternally perfect one, which illuminates even the means of knowledge, shine upon us! — so we pray to that <s>Śaṃbhu</s>. ||
He, the [cosmic] administrator of the three worlds, whose administration is effortless — whose power is concealed by <s>māyā</s> alone — we adore that <s>Hara</s>. ||
Homage to <s>Bhava</s> who, though one, became many through <s>māyā</s>; who though many, shines as one in his own nature. ||
We know the nature of the all-pervading Lord who fills all space, whom <s>māyā</s> cannot touch, who is pure, of the nature of <s>cidānanda</s> (consciousness-bliss). ||
We praise that supreme light by reaching which one does not return — radiant, unfailing, the abode of the bliss of liberation. ||
We praise <s>��ambhu</s> who is unattached, desireless, whose form is <s>sat-cit-ānanda</s> (existence-consciousness-bliss), on whom the entire world depends. ||
May the Lord, the giver of fruits desired and undesired — whose nature cannot be confined by words — protect us! ||

children.text: jñeyas+asi kila ke+api+ete ye tvām+jānanti dhūrjaṭe ||

children.translated_text: He from whom the world proceeds, in whom it abides, and into whom it dissolves — may that <s>Sadāśiva</s>, the ocean of compassion, protect us. ||
Whose glory the <s>Vedas</s> with their auxiliaries proclaim, whose sport is the creation and dissolution of the world — him, <s>Parameśvara</s>, we worship. ||
He who, though transcending all sense-objects, is apprehended through the mind purified by <s>yoga</s> — to that Lord of <s>yoga</s> (<s>Yogeśvara</s>), we bow. ||

children.text: smṛtyā nutyā ca dadate śambhave śam+bhave+abhave ||

children.translated_text: Eternal, all-pervading, subtler than the subtle, free from the six modifications — may that unchanging <s>Maheśvara</s> grant us auspiciousness. ||
The knot of the heart is cut, all doubts are destroyed, and <s>karmas</s> are exhausted — for one in whose heart <s>Śiva</s> shines. ||

children.text: tasya te nātha kāryāṇām+kas+vetti kiyatī gatiḥ ||

children.translated_text: We extol <s>��aṃkara</s>, by meditating upon whom the impurities of <s>karma</s> are destroyed, and the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is realized. ||
He in whom the world-appearance arises like reflections — without touching his nature — to that spotless mirror-like <s>Śiva</s>, homage! ||

children.text: iti śaktilatā yasya puṣpitā pātu+asau bhavaḥ ||

children.translated_text: He by whose thought alone this universe of movable and immovable [things] has been projected — to that omniscient Lord, we bow. ||

children.text: namas+stutau smṛtau dhyāne darśane sparśane tathā |
children.translated_text: Whose <s>śakti</s> alone, in the form of <s>māyā</s>, creates, sustains, and dissolves the [three] worlds — to that self-luminous one, homage! ||
He who is the supreme reality, the cause of all causes, beyond speech and mind, the support of the universe — to that <s>Parameśvara</s>, homage! ||
Like space, he is not stained by the faults of what he pervades; like the sun, he illuminates [all] without partiality — to <s>Śiva</s>, homage! ||
The one Lord who, present in all beings, appears as if many due to the limiting adjuncts of <s>māyā</s> — to that one reality, homage! ||
He whose form no eye has seen, no mind has grasped, no speech has reached — to that inconceivable <s>Śambhu</s>, homage! ||

children.text: krameṇa karmaṇā kena kayā vā prajñayā prabho |
children.translated_text: Smaller than the atom, greater than the greatest, hidden in the cave of the heart of beings — to that <s>Maheśvara</s>, homage! ||
We worship the Self-luminous one, the witness of all, the substratum of all, the eternal, beyond the darkness of ignorance. ||
Homage to him by whose grace alone the bound soul crosses the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> and attains the shore of liberation. ||
He whose body is the universe, whose <s>ātman</s> is consciousness, the Lord of all lords — may that <s>Śiva</s> bestow upon us supreme bliss. ||

children.text: ārambhe bhava sarvatra karma vā karaṇādi vā |
children.translated_text: He who is praised by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Indra</s>, served by all the <s>devas</s> — to that Lord of the <s>devas</s>, homage! ||
He whose lotus feet are meditated upon by yogīs, from whose remembrance all sins are destroyed — may that <s>Śaṃkara</s> protect us. ||
He by whose will alone the entire world-process goes on, without whose grace not even a blade of grass moves — to him, homage! ||
Not the object of the senses, not the object of inference, knowable only through revelation and grace — to that <s>Paramaśiva</s>, homage! ||
He who remains as pure witness when the three states — waking, dream, and deep sleep — arise and dissolve — to that fourth (<s>turīya</s>), homage! ||
Though actionless, he is the prime mover; though changeless, the cause of all change — to that paradoxical <s>Maheśa</s>, we bow. ||
He from whom <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s> flow — the giver of the four human goals — to that beneficent <s>Śiva</s>, homage! ||
We worship the five-faced one whose five activities — creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment, and grace — govern the universe. ||
He who dwells in the hearts of all beings as the inner controller, yet remains untouched by their <s>karmas</s> — to him, homage! ||
He who is the supreme bliss itself, attaining which there is no return — may that <s>Parameśvara</s> be our refuge! ||

children.text: nirdvandve nirupādhau ca tvayi+ātmani sati prabho |
children.translated_text: Homage to the Lord of <s>Umā</s>, whose nature is pure consciousness, free from all limiting adjuncts, the bestower of liberation. ||
He who makes the mute eloquent and the lame cross mountains — to that ocean of compassion, <s>Śaṃkara</s>, homage! ||

children.text: yā yā dik+tatra na kva+asi sarvas+kālas+bhavanmayaḥ |
children.translated_text: The yogīs see him in the cave of the heart through the eye of knowledge; the devotees see him everywhere through the eye of love — to that <s>Śiva</s>, homage! ||

children.text: iti labdhas+api karhi tvam+lapsyase nātha kathyatām ||

children.translated_text: He whose glory cannot be measured by the mind, whose nature cannot be described by speech — to that infinite one, homage! ||
Beginningless, endless, the one without a second, the support of all, beyond all attributes — to that <s>Brahman</s> who is <s>Śiva</s>, homage! ||
He who, though omnipresent, appears as if limited; though eternal, appears as if born — to that Lord of <s>māyā</s>, homage! ||
Homage to <s>Hara</s> who destroys the tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> with its roots, by the fire of knowledge ignited by the wind of dispassion. ||
He whose devotees never fall into evil — who protects those who take refuge in him — to that refuge of the refuge-less, homage! ||
We praise the supreme <s>Śiva</s> who, though having unlimited <s>śakti</s>, remains ever in the repose of his own blissful nature. ||
Homage to you, O <s>Bhava</s>, who though desireless are the bestower of infinite desires, and who though beginningless are the enjoyer of the universe. ||

children.text: anāditve+api viśvasya bhoktre bhava namas+astu te ||

children.translated_text: We praise the Lord who is the root-<s>prakṛti</s> (primal nature) of the origin of the three worlds; from whom, who is of complete <s>dharma</s>, who would not desire benefit? ||
Even in great calamities, when minds are muddied by the flood of delusion, they become clear upon his remembrance — that <s>Śiva</s> we praise. ||
O Lord! Your sovereign power alone is unbreakable here, by whose will the dissolution and creation of the three worlds are extended. ||
He — the God toward whom even an evil-doer's [act of remembrance] becomes the supreme good deed; since the goodness of good deeds comes from no other — you are He, O Lord! ||

children.text: eṣa muṣṭyā gṛhītas+asi dṛṣṭas+eṣa kva yāsi naḥ |
children.translated_text: 'He is grasped with a fist! He is seen! Where will he go from us?' — thus, those blessed ones inflated with the <s>rasa</s> (essence) of devotion run after <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (<s>Śiva</s>). ||

We praise you, who are beyond the beyond of the essence of the <s>Ṛg</s>, <s>Yajus</s>, and <s>Sāman</s> [Vedas] — whose <s>Veda</s>-natured [consort], the unknowable one, is indeed profoundly beautiful! ||
You are the creator at the beginning and the end of the universe, O <s>Parameśvara</s>; whatever community of <s>dharma</s> has proceeded forth — how could it not be from you? ||
Homage to you who, having manifested and shattered the confusion of those bewildered in <s>saṃsāra</s>, reveal the knowledge-bliss that is beyond duality, O God. ||
Whose boundary could be reached by what aspirations? — [that <s>māyā</s> whose limit is unreachable] — may <s>Śiva</s>, who robs that <s>māyā</s> in a single blink, protect us! ||
The profound course of <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), the supreme glory of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),
the highest pinnacle of desirelessness — You, O Lord, are the master of those who bear these.
You are <s>Brahman</s> even to <s>Brahmā</s> himself; of what ruler are You not the ruler?
Who knows how great You are, O You who are the auspiciousness of the world's auspiciousness?
What need is there of other kinsmen, or of friends, or of masters?
In every circumstance, O Lord, You are my deliverer from the ocean of worldly existence.
Victorious are the divine drops of nectar,
drawn by the power of <s>Śaiva-yoga</s>, capable of washing away the stain of delusion and <s>māyā</s> (illusion).
He whose splendor, the inspirer of thoughts, is sung by the <s>Gāyatrī</s> —
may that Lord also impel our thoughts onto the righteous path.
O <s>Aṣṭamūrti</s> (Eight-formed One), will You not grant us eternal abode in even one of Your forms?
Or perhaps, being pleased, You will do everything.
The true nature of things generally produces practical results,
but even Your mere name, O Lord, grants attainment up to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).
The power by which You conceive ever-new states

children.text: śaktis+yā te tayā nātha kas+manasvī na vismitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: of this wondrous world, again and again — O Master, what wise person is not amazed by that?
To make the difficult easy, to turn sorrow into happiness —
the mere remembrance of Him alone is heroic; we remember that enemy of <s>Smara</s> (Desire, i.e., <s>Śiva</s>).
Victorious are the songs whose subject is the Supreme Lord,
by whose very name great souls are covered with the sprouts of horripilation.
If there were another being like You, O <s>Bhava</s>,
endowed with the creation and dissolution of the three worlds arrayed through the deployment of Your own powers —
You are the <s>mantra</s>, You are the one to be counseled, the counselor — who else is there apart from You?
O Lord, give me that <s>mantra</s> by which I may become Your <s>mantra</s> (devotee).
You are of the nature of light, of true resolve; You are the <s>Ātman</s> (Self), and so too am I that Self;
O Lord, is this state of being a worldly being merely a dream? And whence is even that dream in You?
That which is unbreakable, that which is not vulgar, that which is singular and logically sound —
that is the sovereignty of those who have surrendered the fruits of action to You, O Lord.
What calamity is He not capable of destroying? What prosperity is He not capable of granting?
He who is such — that beloved of ours, that god of gods, <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s> (the Bull-bannered One).
For the divine eye of knowledge, blinded by the impurity of <s>māyā</s> (illusion) and delusion,
O Master, devotion to You is the supreme collyrium for its purification.
That which is fearless, that which is full of bliss, that which is one and imperishable —
grant me that state! Come, O God, quickly — what do You wait for?
Ah, the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) is by nature deep and terrible!
Ah, the supreme means of crossing it is none other than <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord)!
Salutation to You who have destroyed Death, the destroyer of <s>Madana</s> (the god of Love),
who bear the <s>Gaṅgā</s> on Your head, and who act in all that is fitting.
For those who seek a state even beyond sovereignty, knowledge, dispassion, and <s>dharma</s>,
O Master, what other supreme refuge is there apart from You?
When You are unwilling, O <s>Śambhu</s>, who has the power to bend even a blade of grass?
But one favored by Your will — who could not bear the yoke of <s>Brahmā</s> (cosmic governance)?
Those whose heads are adorned with the brilliant jewels of their crowns bowed in obeisance to <s>Hara</s> —
to what other could those rich in wisdom bow, or whom else could they not cause to bow?
Free from all disturbance, unwavering, a lake of nectar —
O <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (Matted-haired One), may I dwell in the midst of the ocean of knowledge born of You.
How wondrous that even when merely seen in a painting, or even when only desired in thought,
You, O Master, grant the fruit of ultimate reality in its fullness.
Who is greater than You in virtues? Who is greater than You in being beyond qualities?
Thus, O Master, we bow — should we praise You, or should we not think of criticizing? We cannot fathom.
The fruit of Your grace, which flows even from the mere recitation of the flood of nectar —
who else is able even to drink it, let alone to give it, O Lord of the world?
Since You are the treasure-house for the complete fulfillment of all that is to be desired,
from You I pray only to obtain devotion to You, O Master, by all means.
Salutation to You, the Lord of the three worlds; be favorable to those who worship You;
to the power that bestows the lordship of the three worlds without any obstacle.
When there is doubt as to what is the cause of the complete destruction of afflictions,
O Lord, having ascertained that You are that cause, who would not take refuge in You?
"Having enjoyed pleasures, having abandoned the wandering of worldly existence, I shall attain the supreme state" —
such a hope shines here only for one who has supreme devotion to <s>Śambhu</s>.
O Master, whatever I may do even in a dream, or say, whether good or bad,
through the pride of being under Your control, I am content everywhere in this.
For the mind that races toward Your abode, which is the light of all lights,
O Lord, I consider that the touch of darkness is like the younger brother of a barren woman's son (i.e., utterly impossible).
I consider that even one whose footstep is placed on the auspicious path of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation)
has this wish standing firm: "I shall serve <s>Śiva</s>."
In the activities of sustenance, creation, and dissolution of the three worlds here,
O Lord, Your power alone is the independent instrument — You see it as self-governed.
Who in the three worlds is a protector who has not been scorched by the three afflictions?
Salutation to You who are that lake of nectar of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation).
Even artificial devotion to You produces genuine fruits;
if it were without pretense, let it be told by You what its fruit would be!
That eye by which You are seen, that path by which You are reached,
that fruit, O Unborn One, which has sprung from the wish-fulfilling tree of narratives about You.
The highest good is precisely this — the abiding in You who are above all goods;
for the removal of obstacles to that, You, O Lord, are my refuge.
Ah, how supremely sweet is the nectarean flavor of the hope born of serving <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),
which is ever renewed at every moment of time and never grows old!
Again and again, untiringly, through hundreds of cosmic cycles fashioning the three worlds by creative acts,
yet remaining beyond all conceptual determination — victorious is that single Unborn One.
When shall I come to stand before You, O God,
with the lamp of knowledge that burns away the wick of worldly impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) soaked in the oil of impurity?
If You would make Your abode even for a single moment
in the mind whose faults have been destroyed, O <s>Śambhu</s>, what would You not accomplish then?
"I am blessed, I have fulfilled my purpose, I am great" — such a conviction
becomes well-founded for one whose support is You, O Lord.
You Yourself are the doer of everything, auspicious and inauspicious alike;
but devotion to You, O Lord, is the mother of the auspicious alone.
O Lord, does Your mind become clear and then You enter it, or
does it become clear because of Your entering? — thus people waver in doubt.
But the firm conclusion here is this: Your presiding over the mind
is itself the clarity of the mind, O Lord; that is the <s>siddhi</s> (attainment), that is the supreme state.
My speech, mind, action, and body, O Lord —
by Your grace, may all that become adorned solely with devotion to You.
This <s>Stavacintāmaṇi</s> (Hymn-Jewel), which grants the fruits of abundant desires,
a dwelling of the splendor of devotion to <s>Śambhu</s> — <s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s> composed it.
